headline: Signs It Is Time to Call a Professional for a Custom Tile Shower Installation
articleBody:
Tiling a shower requires strict precision, specialized materials, and skilled waterproofing. Certain complex features and warning signs indicate it is time to bring in an experienced remodeling contractor.

When Professional Guidance Helps
- Curbless or zero-entry designs: Lowering or eliminating the shower curb requires modifying subfloor framing and recessing pans to maintain proper slopes without flooding bathroom floors.
- Relocating drain lines: Shifting a drain requires cutting subfloors, setting appropriate pipe pitches, and tying into primary waste stacks according to local codes.
- Adding built-in benches and recessed niches: Every horizontal shelf or nook creates potential water collection points that require seamless waterproofing membranes to prevent internal leaks.
- Upgrading to a steam shower: Steam applications demand specialized vapor-retardant membranes with specific permeance ratings and complete ceiling enclosures to protect wall cavities.
- Uneven or out-of-plumb framing: Older framing must be straightened and reinforced before setting tile backer board, or your tile lines will buckle and crack over time.
